title: the Bhagavata's tenth book continued
hook: a princess is about to be married to the wrong man, so she writes a letter and finds someone to carry it

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Bhagavata's tenth book continued with a chase: Krishna running unarmed into Muchukunda's cave, and the name Ranchhod. Which argument did you walk away from? Day nine hundred eighty-four.

A letter is traveling by road from the kingdom of Vidarbha to the city of Dwaraka. The man carrying it is an old brahmin, trusted, sworn to deliver it into one pair of hands. The woman who wrote it is the king's daughter, Rukmini. Her brother has arranged her marriage to a king she doesn't want: Shishupala, the man we met earlier this year at Yudhishthira's great rite. The wedding is coming. Her family has decided. And Rukmini has decided too, quietly, on her own. Today, what she wrote.
screen: `A LETTER ON THE ROAD TO DWARAKA.` → `A WEDDING SHE DIDN'T CHOOSE.` → `RUKMINI HAS DECIDED.`

segments.voice: In Dwaraka, Krishna receives the brahmin, washes his feet, feeds him, and only then asks why he's come. The brahmin hands him the letter, and the Bhagavata lets us read it, in paraphrase. I have heard of your qualities, Rukmini writes, and hearing them, my mind has gone to you and won't come back, and I've set shame aside. I have chosen you. Come and take my hand. Don't let the king of Chedi take what is yours, like a jackal stealing a lion's share. Then she does something practical. She gives him a plan. Come to Vidarbha before the wedding, unseen, with your forces. And she knows her own family's customs: before the wedding, the bride walks out of the city to the temple of the goddess Ambika. That's where you'll find me. And if you don't come, she says, I'll give up my life, and keep hoping for you life after life. Look at what kind of devotion this is. Rukmini has never seen Krishna. She has only heard about him. Prahlada's list of the ways of devotion, which we met a few days ago, begins with hearing. But she doesn't stop at longing. She writes, she plans, she risks. And Krishna answers right away: he gets into his chariot that same night. On the appointed day, Rukmini goes to the goddess's temple and prays. She walks out, and he's there. He lifts her into his chariot in front of everyone. There's a fight, and her brother chases them, and loses. In Dwaraka, they marry. Some devotees hear Rukmini as a picture of the soul that has heard of God, chosen God, and taken the first step.
screen: `I HAVE HEARD, AND I HAVE CHOSEN.` · `A PLAN: THE GODDESS'S TEMPLE.` · `SHE NEVER SAW HIM. SHE HEARD.` · `HE COMES THAT SAME NIGHT.` · then, large: `COME AND TAKE MY HAND.`

segments.voice: Sit comfortably, and let the breath be easy. Rukmini's devotion started with hearing. So, for this sit, simply listen. Notice every sound you can: the far ones, the near ones, the sound of your own breath. Don't name them or judge them. Just receive them, one by one. If you pray, you can let a name you love be the sound you return to. If you don't, return to the breath whenever the mind wanders. The bell holds the time.
The Bhagavata's tenth book, continued. Today, Rukmini's letter: devotion that begins by hearing, and then writes, plans and acts.
Your line: the Bhagavata's tenth book continued. Today, take one first step toward something you've chosen in your heart: send the message, make the call. Day nine hundred eighty-four.

howItsDone: Rukmini is worshipped beside Krishna in temples, and some Hindus recite her letter from the Bhagavata, especially when praying for a good marriage; the story is also staged in dance and drama.

pairs: the temple of the goddess Ambika

myth: Rukmini had met Krishna many times before she wrote
she had only heard of his qualities. hearing was where her devotion began.
Rukmini's letter includes a practical plan
come before the wedding, unseen, and find me at the goddess's temple outside the city.
Krishna waits a long time before answering
he sets out in his chariot that same night.

fork.setup: you're Rukmini. your family has promised you to a man you don't want. the wedding is coming. what do you do?
options: write to Krishna, choose him, and give him a plan.
fork.reveal: she writes the letter, sends it with a brahmin, and tells Krishna exactly where to find her: at the goddess's temple.

original.note: Sanskrit, in Devanagari: Rukmini, the princess of Vidarbha, Krishna's queen, worshipped beside him.

trapdoor: what you thought: Krishna rescues a helpless princess.
what it means: Rukmini chooses him first, writes the letter and plans the escape. he answers.
what a scholar hears: the Bhagavata gives her letter in her own voice, a devotee's first step from hearing to acting.
